newsitem.title: UK: Spreads flare as LME copper tightness at fore.
newsitem.headline: Spreads flare as LME copper tightness at fore.

text.p: Copper's nearby backwardation flared dramatically on a hectic London Metal Exchange (LME) midday session as "third Wednesday" pricing on Monday heralded market tightness spanning the next two weeks.
In what traders called an unusually active pricing session, the cash to threes backwardation zoomed out by some $60 from Friday to $205/$215, while cash for a day traded at $19.
Meanwhile pricing purchases swept cash prices from around $2,400 to $2,425 during ring trading.
"I haven't seen the LME this busy in a long time," a trader said, noting heavy cash buying which some estimated at 2,000 lots.
The tightness was expected to persist until after the tight July dates have passed. Traders suspect the market long is an investment interest putting the squeeze on an Asian player among others.
Three months copper was underpinned by the backwardation and finished the kerb $29 firmer at $2,313.
But although prices were holding comfortably above the previous resistance at $2,300, the action was focused on the spreads.
LME chief executive David King said he continues to watch the copper market. He noted that trading during the rings was "totally orderly."
Traders said they expected LME stocks to continue rising steadily due to the higher backwaradation and sluggish seasonal demand. Stocks rose by 2,075 tonnes on Monday.
In other metals, zinc edged close to the key $1,500 resistance level, but stopped just short of piercing it. Still, it ended $12 firmer at a fresh 6-3/4 year high of $1,498.

The market continued to be underpinned by September tightness, which increased on Monday. September/threes were quoted at $16/$18 backwardation and September/day was showing a $3 backwardation. Cash/three month spread was near parity, compared to a $5 contango on Friday.

Aluminium prices were little affected by heavy cash pricing sales, ending $7 firmer at $1,589. A stock drop of 1,625 tonnes, following Friday one-off increase of nearly 7,000 tonnes, reassured the market.
Nickel lost ground in the official ring amid a bout of cash selling, with three months metal slipping $60 to $6,905.
Tin, however, firmed by $60 to $5,610 and lead was lifted by $4 to $671. Alloy was very quiet, easing to $1,438/1,440, versus $1,450.
